title: Stop That Pawn
summary: Let Black promote, then use rook checks to draw the queen onto a knight-fork square.

nodes.question: Must White stop b1=Q immediately?
nodes.explanation: White has Kh8, Rc7, Nc8 and h2 against Ka8 and b2. The win depends on coordinating checks rather than simply blockading the promotion square.

branches.title: Allow promotion and deflect the queen
commentary: Begin from the complete six-piece source board. The h2 pawn is preserved through the combination.
Nb6+ checks the king and changes the knight’s route toward d7 and c5.
Kb8 is the sole legal response to the knight check, placing the king where a later rook check will matter.
Rc3 prepares checks along the third rank instead of trying to stop promotion directly.
b1=Q promotes. Black has a queen, but the king and queen can be drawn onto knight-fork squares.
Nd7+ checks from b6 and restricts the king’s choices.
Kb7 is the source’s central king response, aligning the king above the queen on the b-file.
Rb3+ offers the rook with check. Black must respond to the attack on the king.
Qxb3 captures the rook and places the queen on the knight’s next fork square.
Nc5+ checks Kb7 while attacking Qb3.
Kc6 is the illustrated king retreat, leaving the queen to the knight.
Nxb3 captures the queen. White retains an exact knight-and-pawn win; further conversion is outside this selected line.
branches.explanation: Nxb3 captures the queen. White retains an exact knight-and-pawn win; further conversion is outside this selected line.

branches.title: The king tries the a-file
commentary: Follow the source’s alternative a-file escape after the same promotion setup.
Nb6+ starts with a forcing knight check.
Kb8 is the sole legal king retreat.
Rc3 prepares a lateral rook check after promotion.
b1=Q creates the new queen, without removing the checking combination.
Nd7+ checks and restricts the king.
Ka7 tries to avoid the immediate b-file rook sacrifice.
Ra3+ checks along the a-file and drives the king onto b7.
Kb7 reaches the same deflection setup as the other source branch.
Rb3+ offers the rook on a square the knight can fork.
Qxb3 accepts the rook, relocating the queen to b3.
Nc5+ forks the king and queen.
Kc6 is the same illustrated representative retreat used to complete the fork.
Nxb3 wins the queen, leaving an exactly checked knight-and-pawn win.
branches.explanation: Nxb3 wins the queen, leaving an exactly checked knight-and-pawn win.

branches.title: Start with the rook check instead
commentary: Compare the source’s tempting rook-first approach, which reaches a stalemate defense.
Ra7+ gives check but gives up White’s forced win.
Kb8 steps away from the rook’s a-file check.
Ra6 threatens a later rook check and capture of the pawn, but does not prevent promotion.
b1=Q promotes while preserving Black’s drawing resource.
Rb6+ checks the king and offers a rook-versus-knight liquidation if Black captures.
Ka8 instead keeps the queen available for sacrifice and heads into the corner.
Rxb1 captures the queen but is actual stalemate. Rb1 controls b8 and b7, Nc8 controls a7, and Ka8 is not in check.
branches.explanation: Rxb1 captures the queen but is actual stalemate. Rb1 controls b8 and b7, Nc8 controls a7, and Ka8 is not in check.

exercises.prompt: Why allow Black to get a queen?
exercises.answer: Promotion is not the endpoint. Nd7+ and the rook sacrifice force the king and queen into a knight fork, winning the queen afterward.

exercises.prompt: Why is winning the queen in the rook-first line insufficient?
exercises.answer: Rxb1 removes Black’s final non-king piece while Ra7/Ra6 and Nc8 have confined Ka8. The resulting board is stalemate, so the material gain does not win.

startContext: The complete six-piece source position is visually reconstructed. Two selected knight-first branches let Black promote before deflecting the queen into a fork; the rook-first comparison is actual stalemate. Kc6 and the capture completion use the illustrated representative continuation, without claiming that every defense is shown.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
